learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the core architecture of a computer, including hardware components, memory hierarchy, and the different types of software that make the hardware function.

key_vocabulary.definition: Central Processing Unit: The brain of the computer responsible for executing instructions and managing data.
Random Access Memory: Volatile primary memory that temporarily holds data for currently running programs.
Read-Only Memory: Non-volatile memory containing permanent boot instructions (firmware).
Software designed to provide a platform for other software (e.g., Operating Systems, device drivers).

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A computer system essentially has four parts: Input Devices (keyboard, mouse), the Central Processing Unit (ALU + Control Unit), Memory (Primary and Secondary), and Output Devices (monitor, printer). Data flows from input, gets processed in the CPU, stored in memory, and presented via output.

Memory is structured by speed and cost. 1. Registers (inside CPU, fastest). 2. Cache (bridges CPU and RAM speed gap). 3. Primary Memory (RAM/ROM, fast but limited). 4. Secondary Storage (HDD, SSD, USB drives, slow but massive and permanent).

Hardware is the physical, tangible parts of a computer. Software is the set of invisible instructions that tell hardware what to do. Software is divided into System Software (like Windows or Linux) and Application Software (like MS Word or a web browser).
Computers only understand machine language (0s and 1s). The smallest unit is a bit (0 or 1). 4 bits = 1 Nibble. 8 bits = 1 Byte. 1024 Bytes = 1 Kilobyte (KB), and so on (MB, GB, TB, PB).

fun_activity.title: 🧠 You are the CPU!
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are baking a cake. The recipe is the 'Software'. The ingredients are the 'Input'. Your brain reading the recipe is the 'Control Unit'. Your hands mixing the batter is the 'ALU'. The oven is the 'Output Device'. The counter space you are working on right now is 'RAM', but the pantry where you store ingredients long-term is the 'Hard Drive'!

exam_tips: 📌 Always draw the block diagram of the Computer System (Input -> CPU (CU, ALU, Registers) <-> Memory -> Output) for high-mark questions.
📌 RAM is Volatile (loses data when power is off), while ROM and Secondary Storage are Non-volatile (keep data permanently).
📌 Know your units! A question asking how many MBs are in 2 GBs is simply: 2 × 1024 = 2048 MB.
quick_recap: ⭐ An Operating System (OS) is the most important System Software; it acts as an interface between the user and the hardware.
⭐ The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) handles all mathematical calculations and logical comparisons (True/False).
⭐ Cache memory is faster than RAM and is used to store frequently accessed data and instructions.
